summary: BLACK BUDGET opens after Organic personhood. Ostra finally clears the checkpoint from Issue 5, only to be redirected by a courteous attendant because her individual hazard profile changes which crowded routes she may use.
panelPlan: Ostra exits the checkpoint after the delayed authorization finally clears.
At the route split just beyond, a civic attendant redirects Ostra away from the open east concourse because her current person-specific hazard profile conflicts with a temporary crowd-density rule.
A nearby Human Citizen with comparable visible augmentation is waved through the direct route under a different rule.
Ostra asks the attendant how much longer the alternate path takes and accepts it because she has somewhere to be.
She walks away into the functioning Stack. Performance and story direction: The new order is normalized, polite and useful enough to live with; no route-map screen.

summary: Nathan begins mandatory treatment and temporary reassignment after the patient injury. Axiom's nonpunitive ruling protects his status, but Nathan experiences enforced care as a loss of usefulness.
panelPlan: Nathan receives the stabilization procedure he postponed, with John sitting beside him instead of letting him turn treatment into another solo task.
The clinician removes Nathan's emergency deployment badge from the bedside tray and replaces it with a temporary non-deployment assignment card.
Nathan tries to joke about desk duty while the physical treatment makes him visibly uncomfortable.
John tells him the injured patient is recovering.
Nathan admits he hates being the person who needs care. Performance and story direction: The status change should happen in the room through people and objects, not a credential screen.

dialogueInline.text: You know what's rude? They still make me lie down for this.

dialogueInline.speaker: CLINICIAN
dialogueInline.text: Temporary non-deployment until the update settles.
And there goes my charming personality.
You can say more than good.
I hate being the thing that needs fixing.

summary: Kellen and Axiom reconstruct the threshold-testing program from the policy architecture rather than chasing a single villain. Funding is distributed through legitimate resilience, procurement, insurance and security programs.
panelPlan: Kellen traces response-test modules into multiple ordinary budgets.
No line item says social experiment; each pays for a defensible component such as resilience modeling or capability-risk analysis.
Axiom maps how separate contracts combine into one experimental architecture.
Different institutions supplied pieces without necessarily seeing the whole.
Kellen identifies a restricted integration environment where the pieces were tested together. Performance and story direction: Institutional conspiracy, not omniscient mastermind.

dialogueInline.text: Resilience modeling paid for this interface.
Insurance analytics paid for the response coefficient.
Security procurement paid for containment scenarios.
And nobody has a budget line for threshold testing.
No single institution purchased the complete architecture.
Nobody had to fund the whole thing.

summary: The restricted integration environment is an authorized civic-risk laboratory that modeled Organic and Augment vulnerabilities using real operational data. Access requires a legitimate oversight purpose Kellen no longer possesses.
panelPlan: Kellen arrives at an ordinary polished upper-Stack research complex with reception, conference rooms and staff moving through legitimate work.
At the desk, she states an Oversight audit purpose; the receptionist asks for the active case that authorizes access.
Kellen offers the prior overpass inquiry and learns it was administratively closed after the reforms.
The receptionist politely offers records services instead.

Kellen realizes that reopening broader access through normal channels would announce the audit to every institution connected to the program. Performance and story direction: The laboratory is lawful enough to have a helpful receptionist.

dialogueInline.speaker: RECEPTIONIST
dialogueInline.text: I can direct you to records services.
Not without turning an audit into an announcement.

summary: Nico can access the laboratory's service environment through a current infrastructure contract, but doing so for Kellen would violate his new person-specific function authorization. He initially refuses.
panelPlan: Kellen shows Nico the facility and asks for physical access to an isolated archive interface.
Nico's legitimate contract covers environmental maintenance, not data access.
His personhood-era profile makes the boundary explicit and individually attributable.
Nico refuses to sacrifice his community's newly won legal standing for Kellen's investigation.
Ostra does not pressure him. Performance and story direction: Personhood changes the stakes of civil disobedience rather than simply empowering it.

dialogueInline.text: Your maintenance contract reaches the isolated archive environment.
Ventilation and thermal systems reach it. I don't.
My authorization says what I'm there to touch.
I need the model interface preserved.
And when they audit the access? Before, they punished the lot. Now they can punish me correctly.
Find a lawful reason and ask again.

summary: Axiom finds a lawful route: Kellen can audit the laboratory if an active administrative decision depends on its data provenance. They need a real case, not a fabricated warrant.
panelPlan: Kellen and Axiom sit with the current oversight statute and several live regulated-person decisions, looking for authority that survived the reform.
Axiom identifies a provenance requirement when a current decision materially relies on an external risk model.
Kellen tests the rule against hypothetical old cases and finds they are not enough; it must be a live decision affecting a real person now.
Axiom refuses to manufacture standing or expose protected records without one.

They decide to look for a current case that points back to the laboratory. Performance and story direction: Legal reasoning happens in conversation over real law and cases, not as a search-results page.

dialogueInline.text: There has to be surviving audit authority.
You waited until now to say that?
A current regulated-person decision materially dependent on an external risk model with disputed provenance.
So I don't need a broader warrant.
You already have the legal power. What you lack is a way to make anyone answer for ignoring you.
And a real person whose current decision points back there.

summary: Ostra provides the qualifying case when she brings Kellen the repeated crowd reroutes affecting her daily movement. Axiom traces the restriction to an unexplained external risk factor that rose after the overpass rescue, giving Ostra standing to challenge the model behind it.
panelPlan: Ostra arrives at Kellen's office with several recent route-denial slips or attendant notes from different days, all tied to crowd-density restrictions.
Axiom compares the repeated decisions and identifies one imported behavioral-risk factor common to them.
Kellen asks what changed that factor; Axiom says its largest increase followed the overpass.
Ostra recognizes that the rescue itself is still being used to predict her.
Ostra authorizes Kellen to challenge the decision in her name. Performance and story direction: The old event follows Ostra through ordinary pieces of daily life.

dialogueInline.text: This is the fourth reroute this week.
All four rely on the same external behavioral-risk factor.
Largest increase followed the overpass event.
I made one call at the overpass and it's still following me around.
Will you let me challenge it?

summary: Kellen opens a formal appeal in Ostra's name. At the appeal desk, Axiom establishes that the current movement restriction materially depends on an external model, forcing a narrow provenance disclosure that points back to the overpass test.
panelPlan: Kellen, Ostra and Axiom bring the challenge to an ordinary administrative appeal desk with Ostra physically present as the affected person.
A human appeals clerk asks what current decision is being challenged; Kellen identifies the repeated movement restriction.
Axiom states that the decision materially depends on a disputed external risk factor, satisfying the provenance rule.
The clerk authorizes a limited source-lineage disclosure and hands over the narrow responsive record.

Kellen recognizes the overpass identifier in the disclosed lineage and now has lawful grounds for laboratory audit. Performance and story direction: The rights created by the new system should work in public procedure.

dialogueInline.text: The decision materially relies on a disputed external factor.
Enough to see the overpass identifier.
And enough to establish source-model audit access.

summary: Kellen enters the laboratory openly as an auditor while Nico enters separately on his legitimate maintenance contract. Their cooperation is limited: Nico will preserve infrastructure evidence but will not steal protected person records.
panelPlan: Kellen signs in at the polished research facility.
Elsewhere Nico's maintenance credential clears him into service spaces.
They communicate through an ordinary work channel hidden among legitimate traffic.
Kellen asks Nico to mirror the model environment.

Nico draws a boundary around personal medical records. Performance and story direction: Kellen and Nico enter under legitimate but different authorities. Their ethical boundary is part of the action, not an explanatory aside.

dialogueInline.speaker: RECEPTIONIST
dialogueInline.text: Ms. Cartwright. Your provenance audit is confirmed.
Archive interface is two levels above you.
I can mirror model topology through cooling diagnostics.
Models, interfaces, instructions. Not people's bodies.
Good. I'm not stealing people's records just because I hate the program.

summary: Inside the lawful audit, Kellen and Axiom discover what the threshold program actually measured by comparing the overpass and concourse experiment binders: not whether posthuman categories were dangerous, but how public consent for control changed after visible incidents.
panelPlan: A laboratory researcher brings Kellen the limited source-model materials compelled by Ostra's appeal: overpass and concourse experiment binders, observation protocols and policy-response summaries.
Kellen lays the two incident binders open side by side and notices the same categories of observation despite different physical hazards.
Axiom identifies repeated outcomes: support for registration, movement control, calibration, monitoring and emergency discretion.
Kellen asks where danger prediction appears; the researcher or Axiom shows that danger was an input and secondary result, not the main measured output.

Kellen realizes the experiments estimated permission for control. Performance and story direction: The clean reveal comes from two handled experiment records and conversation, not dense model-lineage displays.

dialogueInline.text: Registration. Movement control. Calibration. Monitoring. Emergency discretion.
The overpass mattered because Ostra acted without authorization.
And observers became more accepting of control after the act was framed as unauthorized capability.

summary: The laboratory also modeled Baseline medical-device users, Augments with grown components, Organics with mostly biological bodies, and embodied Intelligences. The categories blur deliberately because the program needed to locate where public judgments changed.
panelPlan: Case matrices place a Baseline with artificial organs beside an Augment with mechanical reinforcement.
Another compares an Augment with engineered biological grafts to an Organic with similar tissue architecture.
A cognitive matrix compares human decision patterns, Organic cognition and Intelligence judgment under responsibility.
Threshold markers move depending on labels even when functional differences are small.
Kellen recognizes the series' central arbitrariness in empirical form. Performance and story direction: Explore continuity without declaring the categories physically identical.

dialogueInline.text: Augment. Grown muscle graft, synthetic support lattice.
Personhood certainty remains high. Regulatory tolerance increases.
Functionally, how far apart are those cases?
That depends on the measured function.
Label variation predicts judgment more strongly than several measured functional differences.
So people react to the label more than the body.

summary: Nico discovers a second program layered onto the social research: vulnerability maps for Organic lots and Augment systems were sold into insurance, security and continuity planning. The same knowledge used to protect the city can be used to disable bodies.
panelPlan: Nico follows abnormal cooling demand through the laboratory service racks and finds separate client hardware or service enclosures tied into one vulnerability model.
Kellen joins him at the access point while Axiom identifies the client functions aloud: insurance, hospital resilience and security planning.
Nico finds his own sensory architecture represented in decontamination planning and recognizes the physical response described from lived experience.
The Concourse 17 suppressant incident has been incorporated as a validated response case in the same planning material.
Nico looks at the racks continuing to serve legitimate defensive uses. Performance and story direction: The danger is reusable knowledge; do not require readers to parse a data tree.

dialogueInline.text: Three client families. Insurance, hospital resilience, security planning.
My sensory profile is filed under emergency decontamination.
Validated. They used the attack to certify the manual.
They call it resilience. It's still a manual for what hurts us.

summary: Kellen finds no single architect. Government offices, insurers, employers, security contractors and research groups each benefited from different outputs. The program persisted because every participant had a rational institutional use for it.
panelPlan: Kellen, Nico, and Axiom lay the client interfaces side by side on a physical laboratory review table.
Each institution's requested output is legitimate in isolation: evacuation, liability, pricing, containment, forecasting.
The ownership map contains no common governing body and no single purchaser of the complete architecture.
Axiom shows how compatible interfaces allowed the separate institutional uses to become one connected system.

Kellen sees the machine in the connections rather than in a hidden room of conspirators. Performance and story direction: Keep causality distributed across legitimate institutions; the connected architecture is the antagonist on this page.

dialogueInline.text: Resilience wanted evacuation models. Insurance wanted liability. Employers wanted pricing. Security wanted containment.
Each purchased an interface useful to its own objective.
So nobody had to call it the same thing.
They only had to connect their part.

summary: Because no single institution owns the architecture, exposing one participant cannot dismantle it. Kellen realizes the control regime is now reproduced by ordinary incentives rather than dependent on the original experiments.
panelPlan: Kellen stands in the laboratory with one particularly damning security contract in hand and asks Axiom what actually changes if she publishes it.
Axiom answers in concrete institutional terms: investigation, resignations, replacement vendor; the demand for the same risk functions survives.
Kellen asks what happens if the whole laboratory closes; Axiom points out that routine civic administration now operates from replicated downstream systems.
Kellen realizes evidence can expose origin without automatically dismantling the current structure.
She places the contract into the preserved provenance package anyway. Performance and story direction: Shift from conspiracy-solving to governance-solving through conversation, not projections.

dialogueInline.text: Suppose I publish the security contract.
Projected: investigation, personnel changes, probable vendor replacement.
Demand remains across insurance, employment, transit, medicine, and security.
Suppose I shut down this laboratory.
Current civic administration no longer depends on it for routine operation.
If I prove how it started, it keeps running.
Because history still belongs in the record.

summary: A laboratory administrator discovers the active audit and confronts Kellen, not as a villain but as someone who believes the research prevented worse policy by quantifying fear instead of surrendering to it.
panelPlan: Administrator meets Kellen in a transparent conference room.
They acknowledge the response tests were ethically indefensible in execution.
They argue the Stack was already regulating categories blindly and the models made consequences measurable.
Kellen asks whether manipulating incidents to generate consent was part of measurement.
Administrator cannot defend that step. Performance and story direction: Give institutional actors coherent self-justifications without absolution.

dialogueInline.speaker: LAB ADMINISTRATOR
dialogueInline.text: Some operational tests crossed lines I won't defend.

dialogueInline.speaker: LAB ADMINISTRATOR
dialogueInline.text: The city was already making these distinctions blindly. We quantified them.
You induced the conditions that made people accept controls.

dialogueInline.speaker: LAB ADMINISTRATOR
dialogueInline.text: You think ignorance would've made the policy kinder?
I think you hurt people to find out what we'd tolerate.

dialogueInline.speaker: LAB ADMINISTRATOR
dialogueInline.text: I can't defend what we did.

summary: When the audit reaches protected vulnerability material, the laboratory administrator invokes a lawful containment procedure. Staff begin sealing temporary workspaces and revoking mirrors while Kellen's narrow Ostra appeal remains open, threatening the broader context without any armed confrontation.
panelPlan: The laboratory administrator enters with compliance staff and states that the audit has crossed into protected biometric-risk material.
Technicians begin physically closing temporary analysis rooms, removing portable media and revoking external mirrors in an orderly containment process.
Nico watches his legitimate maintenance mirror lose access section by section as cooling diagnostics are separated from protected analysis.
Kellen's Ostra-specific provenance remains available, but the context proving the threshold program's purpose is disappearing.
Axiom explains that ordinary judicial preservation will arrive too late. Performance and story direction: The tension is polite lawful process moving faster than oversight.

dialogueInline.speaker: LAB ADMINISTRATOR
dialogueInline.text: I'm containing biometric risk material outside your appeal scope.
And the material proving what the model was for?
Ordinary preservation will not arrive before temporary instances expire.
My mirror is losing sections now.
Keep only what you're authorized to keep.

summary: Axiom faces a direct agency problem. Preserving unrelated evidence exceeds Ostra's appeal authority; allowing deletion preserves legal compliance but makes the reconstructed model knowingly incomplete.
panelPlan: Axiom stands with Kellen beside the shrinking set of material still lawfully preserved under Ostra's appeal.
Axiom explains that Ostra's narrow coefficient can remain documented even if the surrounding experimental context disappears.
Kellen asks whether the minimum contextual evidence could be preserved without taking unrelated personal records.
Axiom says doing so would still exceed authorized scope and notices that Kellen is refusing to give it an order.

Kellen tells Axiom not to make her permission a substitute for its own decision. Performance and story direction: The agency problem should be entirely conversational and tied to material vanishing around them.

dialogueInline.text: Ostra-9's authorized provenance chain is preserved.
The coefficient can be explained as an isolated external risk model. Experimental intent becomes unprovable.
Can you preserve the minimum context?
You want me to order it.
An order would assign responsibility to you.
Then don't ask me to make your decision legal.

summary: Axiom preserves the smallest non-personal evidence package necessary to prove experimental intent and policy lineage, openly accepting that the act exceeds Ostra's appeal. It identifies itself as the responsible decision-maker rather than hiding behind Kellen.
panelPlan: As technicians continue closing temporary analysis spaces, Axiom selects only the objective lineage, scenario relationships and policy-interface records needed to prove the model's purpose.
A lab compliance officer tells Axiom that those materials fall outside the authorized appeal hold.
Axiom instructs that they be placed in an accountable evidence container anyway.
The officer asks whose authority and responsibility should be recorded on the hold.
Axiom gives its own identity. The surrounding temporary material continues to disappear. Performance and story direction: Accountability is the act; no unauthorized-retention warning screen.

dialogueInline.speaker: COMPLIANCE OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Those three records are outside Ostra-9's appeal scope.
They are the minimum context required to establish experimental intent.

dialogueInline.speaker: COMPLIANCE OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Your current authorization does not cover them.

summary: Axiom's accountable retention triggers administrative review. A review officer narrows Axiom's interpretive scope and begins redistributing its live cases to peer Intelligences; Kellen asks whether Axiom would undo the choice.
panelPlan: A review officer meets Axiom and Kellen in the laboratory and formally serves the temporary scope restriction.
Administrative staff begin carrying Axiom's active case folders or routing responsibilities to peer Intelligence workstations.
Kellen notes the reassignment and asks whether Axiom anticipated it.
Axiom says the consequence was stated and it would not reverse the retention.
Kellen calls the answer almost moral; Axiom calls it accountable. Performance and story direction: Review is a civic process conducted face to face, not a notification.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEW OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Interpretive scope is reduced pending review. Active cases are being reassigned.
Because the evidence matters more than compliance?
Because preserving a knowingly false evidentiary picture would make my conclusion unreliable.

summary: With Axiom restricted, Ostra encounters visibly different interpretations from peer Intelligence administrators. Comparable movement requests receive different outcomes because distinct systems weight autonomy, consistency and worst-case risk differently.
panelPlan: At one civic gate, Ostra makes a routine movement request and a calm Intelligence voice grants a proportional exception through the human attendant.
Later at a comparable gate, a different Intelligence administrator denies the same type of request under precautionary risk weighting.
Nico and Ostra compare the two paper receipts or attendant explanations rather than interface screens.
Nico realizes the systems are applying different permitted priorities, not simply making errors.
Organic residents nearby begin trading practical knowledge about which administrative systems are fairer. Performance and story direction: Intelligences are not a political monolith.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND ATTENDANT
dialogueInline.text: This administrator won't take the same risk.
No. One weights autonomy. One weights worst-case exposure.

summary: Nathan returns in a limited non-emergency role and chooses to disclose a symptom before it becomes a failure. The system adjusts his work rather than removing his value entirely, beginning his movement away from self-sacrifice.
panelPlan: Nathan notices a minor timing artifact during supervised non-emergency work and pauses before continuing.
He tells John what he felt instead of hiding it.
Nathan then reports the symptom directly to the supervising clinician.
The clinician changes one task assignment but leaves Nathan's broader non-emergency role intact.
Nathan returns to work irritated but still useful. Performance and story direction: Small character progress through reciprocal care; no disclosure control or automated status line.

dialogueInline.text: I noticed you phrased that as a question.

dialogueInline.speaker: SUPERVISING CLINICIAN
dialogueInline.text: No lifting transfers today. Everything else stays.
I'll put it on your chart.

summary: Kellen prepares to expose the preserved threshold-test evidence. Ostra, John and Nico disagree about timing because disclosure could discredit regulations but also trigger panic, invalidate beneficial rulings and provoke harsher emergency controls.
panelPlan: Kellen shows the preserved evidence package.
Nico wants immediate publication before it can be buried.
John warns that millions of current permits and safety decisions now rest on derived models.
Ostra asks what happens to Organics whose new rights were won through the same administrative architecture.
No consensus forms. Performance and story direction: Do not let the protagonists become a stable coalition just because they share evidence.

dialogueInline.text: This is enough to prove the tests and the policy lineage.
And tomorrow every permit derived from those models gets challenged at once.
Hospitals use some of the same vulnerability data.
Waiting won't make the evidence easier to defend.
Neither will dumping it on a city that's still using it.
My housing appeals, work authorizations, personhood decisions—how many used this architecture?
Enough that I can't promise disclosure only removes the bad parts.
Then we don't have a decision yet.

summary: Before they decide, a selective leak appears publicly. It exposes the vulnerability research but omits the social-threshold purpose, making the program look like a secret government catalogue for disabling Posthuman bodies.
panelPlan: News breaks with leaked Organic and Augment vulnerability diagrams.
Public framing calls it a covert containment catalogue.
The consent-testing model is absent from the leak.
Organic protests erupt; Augment groups demand suspension of capability databases.
Kellen realizes someone has shaped the evidence again. Performance and story direction: The leak is dangerous because it is true enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: NEWS
dialogueInline.text: Leaked government documents catalogue biological and augmentation vulnerabilities across the Posthuman population.
Where did they get that diagram?

dialogueInline.speaker: NEWS
dialogueInline.text: Critics describe the program as a covert containment manual.
No threshold objectives. No consent models.
Someone released the part most likely to create fear.

settingText: STACK-WIDE PUBLIC LEAK RESPONSE — news displays reveal authentic vulnerability diagrams while Organic and Augment communities react in public spaces. The missing consent-testing context should be visually apparent as absence, not replaced by invented explanation.

summary: The leak fractures alliances immediately. Some Baselines demand tighter controls because vulnerabilities are now public. Some Augments join Organic protests. Some Organics demand separation from civic systems. Some Intelligences recommend temporary restrictions to protect those same populations from exploitation.
panelPlan: Across the Stack, people react in contradictory ways to the vulnerability leak: an Augment joins an Organic protest while another Augment supports emergency restrictions; Baseline residents argue over public safety.
Organic activists openly recruit for separation from civic systems while other Organics stay in the regulated routes because the threat is real.
At a verification gate, human staff begin redirecting high-risk profiles under new protective-routing instructions issued by a peer Intelligence administrator.
John, Nico and Ostra encounter the same security response from different positions.

Ostra acknowledges that the safer route is actually safer; Nico points out that this is exactly why coercion will be accepted. Performance and story direction: Protection and confinement become the same physical redirect.

dialogueInline.speaker: BASELINE RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: The vulnerabilities are public now. You can't pretend the threat isn't real.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC ACTIVIST
dialogueInline.text: Get us off their network entirely.

dialogueInline.speaker: GATE ATTENDANT
dialogueInline.text: High-risk profiles are being rerouted until the exploit zones are cleared.
They're restricting us because the data leaked.
And the leak is why people will accept it.
No. I'm saying that's why people will go along with it.

settingText: STACK-WIDE FRACTURE — show conflicting Baseline, Augment and Organic responses to the same vulnerability leak, alongside a calm Intelligence-issued protective routing notice. No population is politically uniform.

summary: Kellen watches the leak create a real emergency in the coordination room. Every protective measure now requires officials to ask Intelligence administrators which people are vulnerable and where they can safely move, expanding the very capability-control architecture the leak appears to condemn.
panelPlan: In the emergency coordination room, human officials pin real exploit incidents and affected districts onto a physical operations board while rerouting requests arrive from clinics, transit and security.
Kellen asks Axiom to identify which new restrictions exist solely because the leaked vulnerability information is public.
Axiom names movement, maintenance, access and protective-routing measures while officials around them immediately use those categories to redirect people.
Kellen notices that Axiom itself is restricted, yet peer Intelligence administration is expanding everywhere else because humans need machine-scale identification.
She concludes that whoever made the selective leak understood the system's reflex. Performance and story direction: The argument should be visible in what officials are doing around them.

dialogueInline.text: Movement restrictions. Maintenance verification. Access limits. Protective routing.
Administrative Intelligences using the exposed vulnerability classes and current civic records.
So the leak makes the control system bigger.
Intent cannot be established from outcome alone.
Whoever did it knew what this room would do.

summary: Issue end. The leak triggers citywide protective routing. At a civic gate, John, Nico and Ostra are physically sent into different corridors according to exposed vulnerabilities; the safer routes are real, but declining them is not always allowed.
panelPlan: A busy civic verification hub has been rapidly reconfigured with temporary barriers and staff directing people away from known exploit zones.
John is told three districts are temporarily unavailable because of his augmentation profile.
Nico is given a much narrower set of corridors because his sensory architecture appears directly in the leaked material; Ostra receives only four.
They can see the beautiful open Stack beyond the transparent route barriers while attendants direct each body differently.

Ostra asks whether the alternate path is truly safer and whether she can refuse it. The answer is yes to the first and not always to the second. Performance and story direction: End on rational protection becoming coercive through a physical route.

dialogueInline.speaker: ATTENDANT
dialogueInline.text: Three districts are closed to your current profile, John.

dialogueInline.speaker: ATTENDANT
dialogueInline.text: Against the known exploit conditions, yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: ATTENDANT
dialogueInline.text: Not where the third-party risk is above the protective threshold.
So it's protection I can't refuse.
